structuredContent.governing_intent: Create a single CANDIDATE pre-Python architecture/design document for the community-learning contribution model, limited to docs/architecture/pre-python-gate/community-learning.md plus local packet/readiness evidence, carrying forward existing authority without implementing or approving runtime behavior.
structuredContent.summary: The work is a cohesive documentation BIU: synthesize cited local baselines and binding architecture authority into one reviewable candidate design artifact covering consent states, sanitized contribution semantics, privacy/local-first defaults, retention/query/poisoning/provenance controls, human-approved learning, external sharing configuration, examples, limitations, source mapping, and unresolved Founder decisions. The supplied text establishes scope, exclusions, authority boundaries, and observable acceptance criteria.
implementation_unknowns: Exact contents and locations of the named source materials must be found in the local baselines during drafting; the readiness input reports their existence but does not provide their text beyond the included authority excerpts.
The drafter must determine the repository’s existing packet/readiness evidence conventions and documentation checker expectations, if any, for artifact-specific coverage.
The drafter must map source sections to invariants without independently reinterpreting or adopting neighboring candidate documents as approved authority.
The drafter must identify whether any material Founder decisions remain unresolved after source review and record them as candidate/open decisions rather than silently resolving them.
structuredContent.verification_assessment: Acceptance is observable through document review: the candidate artifact can be checked for required invariants, explicit OFF/SANITIZED/PUBLIC_REPRODUCIBLE consent semantics, separate sanitized contribution object, no opt-out penalty, local/shared retention separation, configurable external sharing, provenance/query/poisoning controls, human-approved learning, successful and failing examples, source/invariant mapping, limitations, and unresolved Founder decisions. One independent content review against the supplied authority and source rows is meaningful because the output is a single design document with no operational side effects.
material_risks: The document could accidentally present candidate architecture as Founder-approved or API-stable rather than explicitly CANDIDATE.
The drafter could invent new privacy/security/storage semantics instead of carrying forward cited decisions and marking unresolved choices for Founder review.
The document could over-adopt EOS candidate material or neighboring documents as binding authority despite the stated conformance-pin limitation.
The design could blur private operational records, durable evidence, and shared community-learning contributions, undermining the required privacy/local-first separation.
The artifact could imply external sharing is a core dependency rather than explicitly configured optional participation.
structuredContent.next_action: Hand off for documentation-only drafting of docs/architecture/pre-python-gate/community-learning.md and any permitted local packet/readiness evidence, followed by artifact-specific checks and independent content review.
structuredContent.rationale: The controlling condition is READY because the task has a clear bounded outcome, explicit authority and exclusions, known acceptance criteria, no required implementation or external service access, and no material owner decision that prevents drafting a candidate. Remaining uncertainties are engineering/document-research tasks about locating and mapping sources and following local documentation conventions; they do not require owner clarification before producing a reviewable candidate artifact.
